scope: Independent CPU/source integration review of native request loading, warmup, exact-token host generator, and retained adapter lifetime. Parent separately reviewed projection branches. This is not generation/device qualification.

tiny_cpu_reproductions.scope: Python integration reproductions against held v2; native formula independently transcribed from pinned lora.verify, not a cross-language execution proof

findings.title: Native adapter ownership identity disagrees with Python completion validator
findings.description: lora.verify hashes the NUL-terminated domain, raw 32-byte payload digest, and exact adapter_config.json bytes. model.owner.adapter retains that fingerprint and native construction publishes it. Python compares this field to the raw payload digest. Real adapter completions fail after expensive inference, even though baseline and synthetic construction fixtures pass.
findings.required_fix: Preserve native ownership fingerprint; compute and separately retain the same fingerprint in Python. Add actual tiny native publishConstruction output consumed by the Python validator, plus changed-config and changed-payload negatives.

findings.title: Validation-only reads runtime_manifest before excluding model payload paths
findings.description: The initial capture(paths["runtime_manifest"]) precedes the model-root forbidden-read guard. A malformed request pointing that field at a small model payload opens it before validation fails. Independent guarded-open fixture proves the ordering; no real payload was accessed.
findings.required_fix: Canonicalize and exclude every declared nonmetadata path beneath model_root before any corresponding capture. Keep only the explicit metadata allowlist and add a forbidden-open test for runtime_manifest, not only files_sha256 members.

findings.title: Unpinned per-model user settings can change arithmetic outside the matched resolved tier
findings.description: The host reads $HOME/.mlx-serve/model-settings.json twice through generic main overrides and native arch parsing. These bytes are not required request/runtime inputs. kv16_expert_bf16 changes the expert output rounding kernel in self.exl3, outside model.tier. Construction publishes model.tier only; the paired comparator can therefore label otherwise identical base/adapter receipts matched even if that external setting changes expert output precision. decode_stack4 and other installed routes also need explicit scope.
findings.required_fix: For the exact supervised path, bypass both generic and arch user-setting readers and record an explicit fixed-default settings policy, or bind one immutable captured settings input and record all arithmetic-relevant resolved choices. Add CPU regression on the actual settings-loading seams and paired policy comparison. Ordinary serving need not change.
findings.proof_scope: Source-level composition proof; no GPU output-difference measurement claimed.

nonblocking_observations: Verified.bind creates four host arrays; retainPairs stores distinct retained handles in model.owned, protecting adapter handles against graph resets. The temporary request arena survives binding and serial warmup and is deinitialized only after Module.init returns. Real MLX device lifetime remains a hardware qualification gate.

Serial warmup uses model.fenceOwned, preserves model/state ownership, releases its temporary state, and disables draft execution while keeping draft weights. It follows the stock cumulative warm-state shape pattern. No additional concrete warmup lifetime blocker was found.

The real host forwards the full prompt through prefillsWholePrompt and uses native begin/forward handover; exact mode disables reserved-token suppression and MTP/drafter selection. EOS is restored from the generator stop state, bounded by cap. Token-0 triple-pad stopping in the existing real generator is rejected by exact stopReason as an incomplete result, not silently counted as a successful fixed-cap generation.

The current host fake tests never consume real native construction output and therefore did not exercise SERVE-V2-01. A full host build and zero/nonzero adapter device parity remain required after CPU repairs.
No trainer-forward equivalence, context/throughput qualification, generated-edit apply/compile/correctness, or benchmark success is established by this review.
